text:
alice: Customer reported 429s yesterday even though the Rate & Quota dashboard shows ~40% remaining for their org. Escalating — they have a production outage. https://redwood-internal/incident/INC-3421 :frowning:
ben: Can you paste the exact API response they got and a sample key? we should avoid sharing real keys here, token-id is fine.
alice: Response body (sanitized): `{
  "error": "rate_limit_exceeded",
  "retry_after": 12,
  "rate_limit": {
    "limit": 600,
    "remaining": 0
  }
}` They sent us a screenshot of the dashboard for org `acme-prod` showing 350/600 used (remaining 250).
dave: Customer says their integration hit a batch job and then started getting 429s for ~45 minutes; they saw spikes around 15:23 UTC.
carla: I pulled the analytics pipeline metrics — ingestion lag spiked during the DB migration last night. There's a ~30–60s Kafka backlog but not 45m. I'm not seeing a total mismatch that big in the pipeline consumer offsets.
ben: Two quick hypotheses: (A) dashboard uses aggregated rolling window (60s) but enforcement uses per-second token-bucket counters replicated across shards, causing transient 429s during sudden bursts; (B) we have a stale TTL on the enforcement service's per/api-key quota override cache.
alice: Customer insists they were well under the quota for the hour. They included a curl reproduction request — want us to repro and give them a timeline to share with their ops team.
ben: I'll check enforcement service counters. Can you run this repro against staging and prod? `curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer token-id" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"input":"x"}' -v` Look for `x-rw-rate-limit-*` headers and 429 body. Also check enforcement logs: `grep "token-id" /var/log/enforcement/* | tail -n 200`
carla: Quick note — dashboard shows the *reporting* side totals which are emitted every 60s. For large bursts we only reflect the aggregate after the next emit window. So the dashboard can look fine while enforcement already returned 429s. That matches the 15–45s window, not 45min. Does the customer have many short-lived keys?
dave: They said they rotate keys every minute for their worker pool, yes.
ben: Aha. Replicated counters combined with per-key sharding + rotation can undercount in the reporting path: a token rotating worker will hit different shards and enforcement may locally exhaust bucket while the central reporter hasn't aggregated the exhausted shards yet. That explains 429s even though dashboard shows remaining.
alice: Is there a short-term mitigation? Customer is asking for something actionable now.
ben: Short term: enable reporting of enforcement-side instantaneous counters into the dashboard for that org (adds a new metric endpoint but cheap). I'll open a PR to add enforcement.counter_{org} as a real-time feed to the dashboard. Should be a 1–2 hour patch with a feature-flag.
carla: I'll add a note on the dashboard UI to show "reporting latency" and a hover explaining the 60s emit behavior so CS can explain to customers.
dave: Please send me a short repro script and ETA so I can update the customer.
ben: Repro script (sanitized): `for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer token-id" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"input":"test"}' & done` Run with parallelism to simulate rotating short-lived keys.
alice: Ben — can you also check if the enforcement TTL bug exists? you mentioned cache TTL mismatch earlier.
ben: Checking now — logs show a recent change: enforcement cache TTL for quota-overrides set to 5m in config v2, but reporter reads cache TTL from v1 (1h). If the customer had a short override removed, enforcement would drop it after 5m while dashboard still reports override until reporter refreshes 1h later -> could cause multi-minute discrepancy. I'm filing GH issue #INF-879.
carla: Confirmed: analytics consumer group lag is fine, but reporting aggregation uses the reporter cache which reloads at 60m in prod (we recently increased it to reduce DB load). That plus enforcement 5m TTL can yield up to ~55m divergence in certain override flows.
dave: That's rough. Customer used an override to temporarily increase quota earlier today and then removed it — they hit 429s ~30m after removal while dashboard still showed the override. Explains their report.
alice: Action items: ben -> patch enforcement feed into dashboard (real-time counter) behind FF (2h). ben -> open INF-879 for TTL mismatch (done). carla -> lower reporter cache refresh to 5m for quota metadata for orgs with recent overrides (1d). dave -> communicate ETA to customer.
ben: I'll put a small-sidecar metric exporter in front of enforcement that emits `enforcement.instant_usage{org}` every 10s to the metrics stream. Deploying to canary now. deploy-bot: canary deploy completed for enforcement-sidecar (rev 2f9c).
dave: Thanks — I'll tell the customer we expect a fix within 2 hours and a dashboard clarification tomorrow.
alice: I'll mark this as P1 until the ETA and follow up with the customer post-mortem once we have timelines.
carla: Putting a note on the dashboard change log and creating a short KB article for CS about reporting vs enforcement semantics.
ben: Follow-up: quick patch merged to add the sidecar exporter. Rolling out to non-prod then prod in 45m. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/2345
alice: Great. I'll DM everyone if the customer reopens. Closing thread once prod rollout verified. :white_check_mark:
